subject: C30
required_fixes: R1 — High: crates/desktop-core/src/authority/inbox_domain.rs:423–437 and :480–497 discard established coverage gaps. Runtime completeness checks failures and pagination but ignores unreported key expirations/inconsistent chart totals; Gateway completeness ignores activity_known(), so missing request/error counts still count as read. observation.rs:155–156 and :419–426 already identify these gaps. Home and completion toasts can consequently announce all sources complete while the Inbox has no corresponding warning. Preserve these source-level unknowns in ProductRead and sourcesMissing. Acceptance: production-interface fixtures with a complete key page containing an unreported expiration, inconsistent Runtime totals, and Gateway usage lacking counts each produce named incomplete coverage and a warn completion; fully reported healthy responses remain complete.

R2 — High: crates/desktop-core/src/authority/observation_domain.rs:450–474 records failed Red Team/model-skill attempts as new timestamped outcomes and replaces previous outcomes; inbox_domain.rs:384–397 treats their mere presence as a read, while :533–542 includes failure timestamps in lastReadAt. A first all-source failure with one of these products therefore invents an older read; a failed product-only recheck can report Done, and later failures overwrite the last successful product outcome. Separate attempt/failure metadata from retained successful data and derive aggregate status across selected products. Acceptance: zero-source initial failures yield Failed with lastReadAt null and an actual failedAt; failed rechecks retain the previous successful data/time and report failure explicitly, including when no Runtime overview exists.

R3 — Medium: apps/desktop/src/v2/home.tsx:86–88 falls through to 'Nothing needs action.' during a fresh tenant's first in-progress read. Independently rendering the production Home with state=reading, lastReadAt=null and no items reproduces this alongside 'Reading…'. Empty unread data cannot establish an all-clear under I4. Acceptance: hold the first read open and verify Home continues to describe unread/in-progress coverage; show an all-clear only after an adequate completed read, with failure/partial states qualified.

R4 — High: apps/desktop/src/v2/store.ts:26–31 and :95–99 store tenant-owned notifications without scope; v2-shell.tsx:93–107 emits snooze titles but its tenant/context cleanup never retires toasts, and toasts.tsx:19–24 renders them globally. A tenant A item title remains visible after switching to B, indefinitely with Reduce Motion. An independent React/jsdom probe reproduced this using the production store, Toasts and the shell's cleanup operations. Bind tenant-owned toasts to their scope and hide or retire them on departure/context retirement. Acceptance: snooze in A, switch A→B→A with normal and reduced motion, and verify B never displays A's item/read notification or stale action.

R5 — High: crates/desktop-core/src/authority/harness_history.rs:821–834 admits a save under State, releases that lock, and only then acquires history_hold; the Discard job at :793–799 can acquire history_hold and delete first. The previously admitted sink then saves the discarded transcript again because save_record has no tombstone recheck. Engine termination with a pending approval can overlap its interrupted-turn save while the guard remains actionable. Serializing file I/O alone does not order admission before deletion. Acceptance: deterministically pause a sink after admission but before history_hold, execute Discard, then release the sink; after settlement and relaunch the record must remain absent. Preserve Archive behavior and truthful removal-failure reporting.

R6 — Medium: crates/desktop-core/src/authority/harness_history.rs:443–475 calculates an outstanding discard problem, but successfully opening any record clears h.problem, and successfully deleting a different record also clears it while history_discard_failures still contains the failed discard. This hides the unresolved removal failure contrary to provenance P35. Preserve outstanding discard failures through unrelated history operations. Acceptance: inject a discard removal failure, then open/close a record and delete another record; the warning remains until the corresponding failed record is successfully removed.
